clue.text: Theologian in box in play

indicators.note: in tells us the theologian's letters sit within the box's letters

parts.note: a file is a box or case for keeping documents
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A divine shut up in a box during a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to play idly with something, or to play the violin.

clue.text: Betrayer Mark takes out dunce's daughter

indicators.note: the mark ousts the daughter and takes her place in the dunce, a replacement

parts.note: a dunce is an idiot
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A man named Mark, a traitor, takes a fool's daughter out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betrayer Mark' reads as a person called Mark; Mark is really SCAR, which replaces the D of IDIOT: I-SCAR-IOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his surname stands for any traitor.

clue.text: Arthurian wife to have food sent over

indicators.note: sent over means turned over, so the word is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: to dine is to have food

explanation.surface: A wife at King Arthur's court has her meal delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is the wife of Geraint in the Arthurian romances.

clue.text: It's prudent to consider carefully

definitions.meaning: an adjective: cautious, done with thought
a verb: to weigh up or ponder at length

explanation.surface: It is wise to think things over thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means careful and unhurried; as a verb, to weigh a matter up before deciding.

clue.text: Cross into Nigeria with FT as arranged for Barclays 1

indicators.note: into says the cross is put inside the rearranged letters
as arranged says the letters of the country and the newspaper initials are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A deal involving Nigeria and the Financial Times appears to be set up for the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is FIDDLE, so the definition reads 'Barclays fiddle', the 2012 scandal in which Barclays traders rigged the Libor interest rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barclays fiddle was the manipulation of interbank interest rates, so the scandal's name names that scheme.

clue.text: See 6
Hot Satan perhaps brings death to Greeks

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A fiery devil might bring death to the Greek people.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanatos is the personification of death in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Husband to writer from the religious community

indicators.note: to here means attached to the end of the writer's name

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, English novelists

explanation.surface: A man married to an author who comes from a strict religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a traditionalist Christian community in North America.

clue.text: Barclays thought him such a geezer — for a time

definitions.text: Barclays thought him such a geezer — for a time

parts.words: Barclays thought him such a geezer — for a time
parts.note: Bob of that surname ran Barclays until the 2012 scandal

explanation.surface: The bank rated its man a top bloke, but only for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Diamond was Barclays' chief executive and resigned over the 2012 rate-rigging affair; 'diamond geezer' is Cockney praise for a great guy.
explanation.definitionFit: The bank's former chief executive bore this surname, and the slang phrase 'diamond geezer' praises a fine fellow.

clue.text: An ancient European, I live right next door to Scotsman

indicators.note: next door to means the Scotsman's name sits right beside the earlier letters

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An early inhabitant of Europe says he lives on the right, next to a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberians were a people of ancient Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: For Inquisition, the One Priest

parts.note: the Spanish Inquisition hints at Spanish, where 'the' is el
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: For the Inquisition, the one priest that matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inquisition' points to the famous Spanish Inquisition, so 'the' is put into Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli was the priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Man who wouldn't be left on the shelf?

definitions.text: Man who wouldn't be left on the shelf?

parts.words: Man who wouldn't be left on the shelf?
parts.note: the ideal partner would never be left behind, and the opposite of left is right

explanation.surface: Who is the bachelor nobody would leave unclaimed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left on the shelf' means unmarried; the joke is that this man is the right one, not left.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal husband everyone hopes to find is the perfect partner, never passed over.

clue.text: Heather in famous commercial battle

indicators.note: in tells us the heather goes inside the famous commercial

parts.note: star as an adjective means famous
ling is common heather
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A heather plant appears in a well-known advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalingrad was the decisive battle on the Eastern Front in the Second World War.

clue.text: Singer sticks on wet tar — that's messy

indicators.note: on means the sticks come first with the rest following

parts.note: rods are sticks

indicators.note: messy says the letters of the two words are in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone sings while pressing poles into fresh, sticky tar, which makes a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Stewart is a British rock singer famous for 'Maggie May'.

clue.text: Material from tomb at Ikatan

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Cloth recovered from a grave at a place called Ikatan.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is a wax-resist dyed cloth from Indonesia.

clue.text: There's no time for standing up Norwegian swimmer

indicators.note: there's no means the named letter is left out

parts.note: hair bristling is standing up

explanation.surface: No time to rise to your feet for a Norwegian swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisling is a small sprat-like fish, canned as Norwegian sardines.

clue.text: Military commander finds range

definitions.meaning: an Ottoman officer of high rank

explanation.surface: An army leader locates a target's range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' is a British word for a cooking stove; the Aga is a well-known brand of one.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga was a Turkish commander, and an Aga is a heavy British cooking stove.

clue.text: Cameron in South of France to return in melancholic state

indicators.note: to return means the whole assembly is turned back to front
in says the Cameron letters go inside the French south

parts.note: sud is French for south
David Cameron was Prime Minister when this was set

explanation.surface: The prime minister goes back to the south of France, feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cameron' looks like a surname to take whole; it stands for his office then, Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down in the dumps is being gloomy or depressed.

clue.text: Flower from French husband so proverbially good

parts.note: mari is French for husband
the saying 'as good as gold' gives the precious metal

explanation.surface: A bloom from a Frenchman, the husband said to be very good.
explanation.definitionFit: The marigold is a bright orange or yellow garden flower.

clue.text: Rude writer is to the point

parts.note: the writer speaking of themself says 'I am', shortened
pertinent means relevant, to the point

explanation.surface: An impolite author claims to be getting straight to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Impertinent means cheeky or disrespectful, a synonym of rude.

clue.text: State needs humour injection

parts.note: a pun is a piece of verbal humour
a jab is an injection

explanation.surface: A country needs a dose of comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjab is a state of India, and a province of Pakistan.

clue.text: Government, Republican, mirrored German affirmation

indicators.note: mirrored means seen as in a mirror, read backwards

parts.note: ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Government by a Republican, echoed by a German yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raj was British rule over India.

clue.text: Katie Price in river

definitions.meaning: the British glamour model's former stage name
the river of the Middle East where Jesus was baptised

explanation.surface: A celebrity model is spotted in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Katie Price is a British glamour model and TV personality who worked under a one-word stage name.
explanation.definitionFit: Katie Price modelled as Jordan, and the Jordan is a river flowing to the Dead Sea.

clue.text: Resolution on pound 6 Barclays were 7

indicators.note: on means the resolution comes after the pound sign in this across entry

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra
an ending is a resolution of a story

explanation.surface: A conclusion about money, and the rate the bank was rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: With 6 as RATE and 7 as FIXING, the definition reads 'rate Barclays were fixing': the interbank lending rate, Libor.
explanation.definitionFit: Barclays rigged the Libor, a benchmark interbank borrowing rate, so this qualifier completes its name.

clue.text: I was leader in bombless state

parts.note: ran means was in charge, led

explanation.surface: A former ruler speaks of a country without nuclear weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombless' is a wry nod to Iran's then disputed lack of a nuclear bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a Middle Eastern country, jokingly described as lacking a nuclear weapon.

clue.text: Rich old girl to make bet

parts.note: to do is to make or perform
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: A wealthy elderly woman places a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow who holds property from her late husband, often a wealthy old lady.

clue.text: Many a Welsh runner in the gloaming

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number
the Usk is a river in Wales; a river runs

explanation.surface: Lots of Welsh athletes are out jogging at twilight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a crossword word for a river: it runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The gloaming is the Scots word for twilight, the dim light of evening.

clue.text: Rand given back to French for the antelope

indicators.note: given back means the name is turned round

parts.note: Ayn Rand, the novelist
la is the feminine French word for the

explanation.surface: South African money returned in exchange for an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rand' wants to be South Africa's currency; it is the novelist Ayn Rand.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Oddly able to enter one country or another

indicators.note: to enter means the selected letters go inside the country

parts.note: Austria is a European country

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: Somehow capable of getting into one nation or another.
explanation.walkthrough: Once Austria is 'one country', 'another' stands for a second country.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a further nation set beside the first, so 'another' country names it.
